title: Oxidation Number
content: The oxidation number (or oxidation state) of an atom represents the number of electrons lost or gained by an atom and can be zero, positive, or negative[cite: 1].

title: Oxidation
content: Oxidation is the addition of oxygen (or electronegative element) to a substance or the removal of hydrogen (or electropositive element) from a substance. It is the loss of electrons by an element, compound or ion, or an increase in oxidation number[cite: 1].

title: Reduction
content: Reduction is the removal of oxygen (or electronegative element) from a substance or the addition of hydrogen (or electropositive element) to a substance. It is the gain of electrons by an element, compound or ion, or a decrease in oxidation number[cite: 1].

title: Redox Reaction
content: Chemical reactions which involve oxidation as well as reduction processes simultaneously are known as redox reactions[cite: 1].

title: Oxidising Agent
content: An oxidising agent or oxidant is an acceptor of electrons and is reduced itself in a chemical reaction[cite: 1].

title: Reducing Agent
content: A reducing agent or reductant is a donor of electrons and is oxidised in a chemical reaction[cite: 1].
